tells.1: Highly symmetrical consequence bullets and generic framing such as “The consequences are significant” give it a templated feel.
tells.2: Some stock phrasing remains, particularly “Agencies bear the cost,” but the prose is mostly direct and natural.
tells.3: Conspicuous casual substitutions—“sit uncovered,” “actually accept,” “bunch up,” “in the loop”—feel like an effort to manufacture human warmth.
tells.4: “This causes four problems” and the uniformly structured bullets make the exposition feel mechanically organized.
tells.6: “What this costs” feels like an editorial flourish attached to an otherwise conventional template.

reason: Version 2 best balances natural language, clarity, and a professional PRD tone; these stylistic impressions do not establish authorship. Version 5 reads like an unfinished draft rather than skilled final copy, and even version 2 needs to distinguish confirmed reassignment from escalation before publication.
